root_idea.summary: The root centers on taking or grasping something through coercion, dominance, and force.
root_idea.development: From forceful grasp, the lexicon extends to violent seizure and assault and to nouns for the act or its occurrence. Broader Classical Arabic uses include might, struggle, anger, figurative assault, work or ability, and several specialized derived applications.

senses.definition: To seize violently, lay violent hands on, or assault.
senses.usage_conditions: Normally used with بِهِ for the person or thing seized. In the Quranic construction نَبْطِشُ الْبَطْشَةَ الْكُبْرَى, it describes making the greatest assault; an alternate interpretation understands the construction as giving power over them to assailants.

senses.definition: Forceful seizure or assault; an overpowering grip.
senses.usage_conditions: Verbal noun of بَطَشَ. In Quranic contexts, the act may be rendered according to its construction as power, force, or grip.
In الْبَطْشَةُ الْكُبْرَى, “the greatest assault,” the referent is explained variously as the Resurrection or the battle of Badr.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take hold of a thing strongly or cling to it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A use of the verb with a thing as its object, with the preposition بِ understood or with the sense of taking and handling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To assault or overwhelm figuratively, as when terrors assail people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative use with circumstances or other nonhuman agents as the assailant.
Said of a hand when it works or labors; figuratively used of a person's activity in knowledge, to labor with extensive ability.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To recover from a fever while still weak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare specialized usage associated with recovery from illness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strive, struggle, contend, or conflict with another to prevail or overcome.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reciprocal construction may describe two people reaching out to seize and assault one another quickly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Might or strength in war or combat; courage, valour, or prowess.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical noun describing a person's martial force or bravery.
An independently attested Classical nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A forceful or violent person; one of great might in seizure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man characterized by severe or powerful seizure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To move with slow, halting steps under a burden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of travelling camels that proceed laboriously with their loads.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of assault or a site characterized by assault.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also reported with the variant مَبْطَشٌ; the plural is مَبَاطِشُ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Forceful seizure and the Quranic greatest-assault construction are represented.
Strong taking or clinging is separately represented.
Figurative assault by terrors is represented.
Working of the hand is covered by the broader work or labor meaning.
Laboring in knowledge with extensive ability is covered by the work or labor meaning.
The specialized recovery-from-fever use is represented.
Striving, contending, and struggling to prevail are represented.
Mutual violent reaching and assault are covered by the reciprocal struggle meaning.

cautions: The Quranic phrase الْبَطْشَةُ الْكُبْرَى has differing reported referents, including the Resurrection and the battle of Badr; the associated verbal construction also has an alternate interpretive explanation.
